poster_title: Human-in-the-loop or AI-in-the-loop? Automate or Collaborate?
authors: Sriraam Natarajan, Saurabh Mathur, Sahil Sidheekh, Wolfgang Stammer, Kristian Kersting
paper_info: 2025, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org)

panels.headline: Clarify the distinction between HIL and AI2L systems
content: HIL systems combine data-driven machine learning with human expertise.
Many HIL systems treat humans as data-labeling oracles or sources of domain knowledge.
Traditional HIL systems often overemphasize the machine component's performance and neglect human roles.
panels.figure_caption: A comparison of human in the loop (left) and AI in the loop (right) systems. In human-in-the-loop systems, AI systems drive the inference and decision-making process, but humans intervene to provide corrections and supervision. In AI-in-the-loop systems, humans make the ultimate decisions.

panels.headline: The term 'HIL' is often misused
content: The term 'HIL' is often misused, as many systems are actually AI2L systems.
Evaluation methods for HIL systems do not adequately account for the human expert's influence.
AI2L systems require a different approach to evaluation and deployment compared to HIL systems.
panels.figure_caption: Examples of subtasks across various domains and their classification as Automate (HIL) or Collaborate (AI2L).

panels.headline: Propose an AI2L perspective
content: Propose an AI2L perspective that recognizes the human expert as an active participant.
Develop evaluation methods that incorporate human-centered metrics such as calibration, fairness, and explainability.
Analyze the conditions under which HIL or AI2L systems are appropriate for different tasks.

panels.headline: Compare HIL and AI2L systems
content: Compare HIL and AI2L systems through detailed examples and case studies.
Evaluate the performance and usability of AI2L systems in real-world scenarios.

panels.headline: AI2L systems are more comprehensive
content: AI2L systems are more comprehensive and faithful in modeling the human-machine interplay.
AI2L systems can lead to more effective and robust AI systems.
Evaluation methods for AI2L systems need to consider human factors beyond traditional metrics.

panels.headline: Designers must understand the conditions
content: Designers must understand the conditions under which HIL or AI2L systems are appropriate.
There is no one-size-fits-all solution for AI system design; the human role is crucial.
AI2L systems offer a promising direction for more effective and robust AI applications.
The paper does not provide specific technical details on how to implement AI2L systems.
The case studies and examples are limited and may not cover all scenarios.
